The '''Cessna Citation Latitude''' is a [[business jet]] built by [[Cessna]].
<section begin=summary/><!--Development-->The Model 680A was announced at the 2011 [[National Business Aviation Association|NBAA]] convention, the prototype first flew on 18 February 2014, it achieved [[Federal Aviation Administration|FAA]] certification on June 5, 2015, and first deliveries began on August 27.
<!--design-->
It retains the  [[Cessna Citation Sovereign|Model 680 Sovereign]] wing, twin [[Pratt & Whitney Canada PW300|P&WC PW306D]] turbofans and [[cruciform tail]] and adds a new stand-up circular [[fuselage]] with a flat floor, which was kept in the stretched, re-winged, and re-engined [[Cessna Citation Longitude]].<section end=summary/>

==Development==

The $14.9 million Citation Latitude was announced by Cessna at the annual [[National Business Aviation Association|NBAA]] convention in October 2011, between the $12.6 million [[Citation XLS]]+ and the $17.5 million [[Citation Sovereign]].<ref name=Flight10oct2011/>
The prototype first flew on 18 February 2014 in Wichita, Kansas.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Trimble|first1=Stephen|title=Cessna completes Latitude first flight|url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/cessna-completes-latitude-first-flight-396082/|access-date=22 June 2015|publisher=[[Flightglobal]]|date=19 February 2014|location=Washington DC}}</ref>
Cessna announced on June 5, 2015, that it had achieved FAA certification for the type.<ref name=Textron5jun2015>{{cite press release |title=Cessna Citation Latitude awarded FAA certification |url= http://txtav.com/en/newsroom/2015/06/cessna-citation-latitude-awarded-faa-certification |location= Wichita, KS |publisher= [[Textron Aviation]] |date= 5 June 2015}}</ref>
On August 27, 2015, Cessna announced the first deliveries had begun.<ref>{{cite press release |url= http://txtav.com/en/newsroom/2015/08/citation-latitude-now-in-the-hands-of-customers-with-deliveries-underway |date= August 27, 2015 |title= Citation Latitude now in the hands of customers with deliveries underway |publisher= Cessna}}</ref>
In 2023, its equipped price was $19.775M.<ref>{{cite news |url= https://infogram.com/bca-table-2023-jets-1ho16vorwrp8x4n |title= Purchase planning handbook - Jets table |date= Second Quarter 2023 |work= Business & Commercial Aircraft}}</ref>

==Design==
[[File:Cessna Citation Latitude N563QS departing Scottsdale Airport, October 2023.jpg|thumb|A Cessna Citation Latitude, registration N563QS, departing Scottsdale Airport, Arizona, in October 2023]]

It keeps the [[Citation Sovereign]] wing, twin [[Pratt & Whitney Canada PW300|Pratt & Whitney Canada PW306D]] turbofans and [[cruciform tail]].
Its newly-designed all-metal stand-up circular [[fuselage]] has a flat floor and seats nine.<ref name=Flight10oct2011>{{cite news|last1=Croft|first1=John|title=Cessna gets attitude with Latitude|url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/cessna-gets-attitude-with-latitude-362864/|access-date=9 April 2013|publisher=[[Flightglobal]]|date=10 October 2011|location=Washington DC}}</ref>

<!--performance-->
Typical missions are 2.0–2.7 hours and with {{cvt|400|knots|mi/h km/h}} block speeds and most operators can fly 5–6 hours at Mach 0.72–0.76 for a {{cvt|2,000|–|2,400|nmi|mi}} range, with short [[takeoff]] requirements and good [[hot and high]] performance.<!--<ref name=BCA22jun2018>-->
A first hour fuel burn of {{cvt|2,000–2,500|lb}} followed by {{cvt|1,600–1,900|lb}} the second hour and fuel burn can reach {{cvt|3,300|lb}} for a 2-hour trip with favorable conditions.<!--<ref name=BCA22jun2018>-->
It lists for $17.5–18 million typically equipped, the same as the [[Embraer Legacy 450]] with a similar flat floor cabin for club four plus two chairs and over 200 miles more range, {{cvt|25–30|knots|mi/h km/h}} higher cruise and [[fly-by-wire]] controls.<!--<ref name=BCA22jun2018>-->
Embraer is firm on list price while Textron [[Price discounting|discount]]s the Latitude by up to 20% for $13.5–14 million to sell three times as many aircraft.<ref name=BCA22jun2018>{{cite news |url= http://aviationweek.com/bca/citation-latitude-bargain-priced-super-midsize-wins-customer-loyalty |title= Citation Latitude: Bargain-Priced Super-Midsize Wins Customer Loyalty |date= Jun 22, 2018 |author= Fred George |work= Business & Commercial Aviation}}</ref>

==Operational history==
[[File:EBACE 2019, Le Grand-Saconnex (EB190620).jpg|thumb|upright|Interior of a Latitude ambulance jet]]

Deliveries to customers began in the third quarter of 2015 and sixteen had been handed over by the end of the year.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://gama.aero/wp-content/uploads/2015ShipmentReport-03212016Ed.pdf |title= 2015 Year End General Aviation Aircraft Shipment Report |date= March 21, 2016 |publisher= GAMA }}</ref>
By May 2018, almost three years since introduction, 124 had been delivered and had logged 80,000 flight hours.<ref name=AINMay2018>{{cite news |url= https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2018-05-28/citation-latitude-clocks-5000-hours-netjets-europe |title= Citation Latitude Clocks 5,000 Hours with NetJets Europe |author= Ian Sheppard |date= May 28, 2018 |work= AIN online }}</ref>

In June 2018, of 129 delivered, {{#expr:129-25}} were in the US, three in Mexico, two each are based in China, France and Turkey, and there was one each in Chile, Paraguay, the Philippines, Poland, Scotland and Switzerland.<!--<ref name=BCA22jun2018>-->
It is used by medium-size corporations, typically flying 200–300 hours per year, and large fleet operators, the largest being [[NetJets]] which booked 25 firm orders and 125 options in 2012 and received 44 aircraft for its U.S. operations and 10 for Europe by June 2018, flying theirs over 1,000 hours per year.<ref name=BCA22jun2018/>
By mid-September, the 136 delivered had logged 115,000 flight hours, and Textron claimed it was outselling the competition by four to one.<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2018-10-11/textron-aviation-optimistic-future |title= Textron Aviation Optimistic for Future |author= Matt Thurber |date= October 11, 2018 |work=AIN online}}</ref>
